title: Most Profitable Path in a Tree
summary: Consider an undirected tree with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, rooted at node 0.
statement: Consider an undirected tree with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, rooted at node 0. Given a 2D integer array edges representing the connections between nodes, and an array of even integers amount indicating the price needed to open the gate or the cash reward at each node, determine the maximum net income Alice can achieve. Alice starts at node 0, while Bob starts at node bob. At each second, both move to an adjacent node, with Alice moving towards a leaf node and Bob moving towards node 0. If Alice and Bob meet at a node, they share the cost or reward equally. Alice stops when she reaches a leaf node, and Bob stops when he reaches node 0. The goal is to find the path that maximizes Alice's net income.
constraints: The undirected tree is rooted at 0; Alice starts at 0 and chooses a root-to-leaf path while Bob starts at bob and follows the unique path to 0.
At a node Alice receives the full even amount if she arrives before Bob, half if simultaneous, and zero if Bob arrived first; negative amounts are costs.
Return Alice’s maximum total over all root-to-leaf paths.
hints: Root the tree to compute each node’s parent and Alice arrival depth.
Walk Bob through parent links and record his arrival time on that path.
Traverse every Alice root-to-leaf path, adding full, half, or zero according to arrival comparison.
Both paths in a tree are unique, so recorded times are exact; maximizing totals at leaves examines every legal Alice choice.
editorial: Both paths in a tree are unique, so recorded times are exact; maximizing totals at leaves examines every legal Alice choice.

tests.explanation: Alice’s best path reaches node 4; applying Bob’s arrival times yields total six.
Alice opens the root before Bob arrives and pays 7280; Bob already opened node 1, so her total is -7280.
